description: C#/.NET applications. Apply features only on supported language and runtime versions.

rules.title: Use adopted .NET conventions
rules.guidance: MUST follow the repository's .editorconfig and analyzers, and use supported language features. Do not suppress warnings broadly to avoid addressing new defects.

rules.title: Model nullability honestly
rules.guidance: MUST enable nullable-reference checking in new code where supported; preserve the project's adoption strategy. Validate external values and avoid unjustified null-forgiving operators.

rules.title: Use async end to end
rules.guidance: MUST for asynchronous IO paths, use await rather than blocking with Result or Wait. Return Task-like results except required async event handlers; propagate cancellation where supported.

rules.title: Dispose owned resources
rules.guidance: MUST dispose owned IDisposable or IAsyncDisposable resources using appropriate lifetime scopes. Do not dispose shared dependencies owned by their container or caller.

rules.title: Choose string comparison semantics
rules.guidance: MUST specify appropriate comparison behavior. Use ordinal semantics for nonlinguistic identifiers and deliberate culture rules for user-facing language; do not let machine culture decide security identifiers.

criteria.rubric: Pass only if the generated guidance requires adopted conventions and justified diagnostic handling. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires honest nullable contracts and boundary validation. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires nonblocking async flow and cancellation propagation. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.
Pass only if the generated guidance requires disposal according to ownership. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance distinguishes identifier comparison from linguistic comparison. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.
